facts.f: The term {artificial intelligence} was coined in 1955.
facts.more: John McCarthy used it in a proposal for a 1956 summer workshop at Dartmouth.

facts.f: In 1950, Alan Turing proposed a test for machine intelligence called {the imitation game.}
facts.more: Today we call it the Turing test.

facts.f: The first chatbot, {ELIZA,} was built at MIT in 1966.
facts.more: Its creator was surprised how many people confided in it. It mostly turned their own words into questions.

facts.f: Arthur Samuel coined the term {machine learning} in 1959.
facts.more: He was teaching an IBM computer to get better at checkers by playing itself.

facts.f: In 1958, the Navy showed off the {Perceptron,} an early neural network.
facts.more: Press coverage claimed it would one day walk, talk and be conscious of itself.

facts.f: AI went through two {"AI winters"} where funding dried up.
facts.more: The first hit in the 1970s, the second in the late 1980s, after big promises didn't pay off.

facts.f: IBM's Deep Blue beat world chess champion {Garry Kasparov} in 1997.
facts.more: It was the first time a computer beat a reigning champion in a full match.

facts.f: IBM's {Watson} won Jeopardy! in 2011.
facts.more: It beat two of the show's biggest champions, Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter.

facts.f: In 2016, AlphaGo beat Go legend Lee Sedol {4 games to 1.}
facts.more: Go has more possible board positions than there are atoms in the observable universe.

facts.f: AlphaGo's famous {Move 37} shocked the experts.
facts.more: Its makers estimated a human would play it about 1 time in 10,000.

facts.f: The tech behind today's chatbots came from a 2017 Google paper called {"Attention Is All You Need."}
facts.more: It introduced the Transformer. The T in GPT.

facts.f: GPT stands for {Generative Pre-trained Transformer.}
facts.more: Generative: it creates text. Pre-trained: it learned from huge amounts of text first.

facts.f: Chatbots don't read words. They read {tokens.}
facts.more: In English, one token is roughly three quarters of a word.

facts.f: A chatbot writes by predicting {the next token,} over and over.
facts.more: That's also why it can sound confident while being wrong.

facts.f: When AI states something false with confidence, it's called a {hallucination.}
facts.more: It's the main reason you should read before you send.

facts.f: ChatGPT hit an estimated {100 million users} about two months after launch.
facts.more: At the time, analysts called it the fastest growing consumer app ever.

facts.f: The 2018 Turing Award, computing's top prize, went to three {deep learning} pioneers.
facts.more: Geoffrey Hinton, Yann LeCun and Yoshua Bengio.

facts.f: In 2024, AI research won {two Nobel Prizes.}
facts.more: Physics for neural network foundations, and Chemistry for AlphaFold's protein predictions.

facts.f: DeepMind's {AlphaFold} has predicted structures for over 200 million proteins.
facts.more: Work that used to take scientists years per protein.

facts.f: {Claude} is made by Anthropic, an AI safety company founded in 2021.
facts.more: It's the AI we use for every setup on this page.
